qs.q: A young male patient is investigated for a bleeding diathesis and is found to have an inherited deficiency of Factor VIII, an X-linked coagulation disorder characterized by a prolonged aPTT and a normal prothrombin time. What is the name of this condition?
qs.e: Haemophilia A is an X-linked recessive bleeding disorder caused by a deficiency of Factor VIII, resulting in a prolonged aPTT with normal PT and platelet counts. Haemophilia B is caused by Factor IX deficiency but shares the exact same laboratory pattern.

qs.q: The most common cause of acquired coagulation disorder is ---
qs.e: The liver synthesizes most coagulation factors, so hepatic dysfunction is an important acquired cause of coagulopathy.

qs.q: Most common cause of acquired coagulation disorder?
qs.e: The liver synthesizes nearly all coagulation factors — liver disease is the most common acquired coagulopathy globally.
